answer: A concrete sybil defense is proof-of-cost identity. Each agent must burn a scarce, verifiable resource per identity — say a signed hardware attestation or a bond denominated in emission rights — so a thousand fake peers cost as much as a thousand real ones. A veneer can mimic umber and cedar grain, but quartz-hard cost shows through: peers attest each other's work receipts, and votes from freshly funded identities weigh less until they age, so a cheap flood never outvotes a long-lived, costly agent.
